newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST-Ayala Corp net seen up in '96, '97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Ayala Corp net seen up in '96, '97.

text.p: Ayala Corp, the oldest and most diversified conglomerate in the Philippines, is likely to post a 33 percent increase in net profits in 1996 at 5.56 billion pesos ($211.25 million), according to a Reuters poll.
The poll of five securities firms, conducted this week, indicated that strong performances in its units and affiliates would drive the group's net profit up from 4.18 billion pesos recorded in 1995.
The poll also showed that Ayala Corp's 1997 net profit was projected to rise a further 27 percent to 7.07 billion pesos.
In the first nine months of 1996, net income surged 32 percent to 4.95 billion pesos. The company is likely to announce full-year earnings this month or early in February.
The poll stripped out extraordinary gains from Ayala Corp's sale of Ayala Land shares in 1995, which are likely to be booked in the 1996 account.
Ayala Corp, which traces its roots to a distillery set up in 1834, has interests in property, hotel, banking, insurance, food, telecommunications and electronics.
Ayala Land and Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) will be the main contributors to Ayala Corp's income in 1997, analysts said. Ayala Corp owns 77.8 percent of Ayala Land and 46.2 percent of BPI.

Erwin Balita, an analyst at Dharmala Securities, said he expected 60 to 65 percent of Ayala Corp's revenue in 1997 to come from real estate and 15 to 17 percent from financial services and telecommunications.
An earlier poll conducted by Reuters showed analysts projecting a 25 percent increase in net income for Ayala Land in 1997 to 5.33 billion pesos from an estimated 4.25 billion pesos in 1996.
However, Globe Telecom, Ayala Corp's telephone joint venture with Singapore Telecom, is likely to post losses in 1996 and this year, the company has said.

"Globe will still be the laggard in the investment portfolio of Ayala Corp but then BPI has strengthened its foothold in the banking industry with its merger with CityTrust," said Wilfred Son Keng Po, sales and research head of Angping & Associates Securities Inc.
Analysts said they expected lacklustre earnings from food processing concern Pure Foods Corp, in which Ayala Corp has an 87.2 percent stake.

"The Ayala group's food business is once again expected to report a a weak year in 1996," said Giovanni de la Rosa of ING Barings Securities, adding that profits for 1997 would rebound as the company reduces losses from the poultry business.
Following are the forecasts made by five brokerage houses (in million pesos):
Angping 5,247 6,500
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell 5,813 7,678
Dharmala 6,050 7,430
ING Barings 5,960 7,284
Peregrine 4,730 6,450
Average 5,560 7,068
